name: cooling_coil_condensate_ratio
title: Condensate ratio and dry-air flow at a cooling coil, and a counter-flow recuperator
summary: Revision exercise with two questions on one heat-pump cycle: (1) a 7 kW cooling coil that dehumidifies air from 28 C/80 % RH to 13 C saturated, solved with two first-law methods (humid-air enthalpies neglecting the condensate, or separate dry-air/vapour/condensate terms), giving the condensate-to-dry-air ratio and the dry-air flow; (2) a counter-flow R113 recuperator of effectiveness 60 % with 5 kPa pressure drops on both sides, giving the outlet temperature T10.

authors: TBD (ULiège course MECA0002; inventory suggests S. Quoilin with repetition assistants N. Paulus and B. Dechesne)
origin.course: ULiège Thermodynamique appliquée (MECA0002), R12 revision session 2022-2023 - exercises from the January 2022 exam

verification.reference: Solution stored in the original EES file (54/54 variables)
verification.notes: Hand-converted from kPa/kJ. compare_solution.py --ees-units: '54 common variables, 12 differ (rtol=0.001)'. The largest deviation, 3.06e-01 on h_a_sec_ex, is the reference-state offset of the Air_ha dry-air enthalpy (+126 kJ/kg CoolProp vs EES; no variable excluded - the difference h_a_sec_ex - h_a_sec_su = -15095 J/kg used by the model is identical in both tools). The remaining deviations are the EES-vs-CoolProp humid-air properties: omega +4.6e-03/+5.2e-03, humid-air enthalpies +3.2e-03, derived results ratio 3.9e-03, m_dot_a 3.3e-03, m_dot_a_bis2 2.5e-03, m_dot_cond 1.5e-03. All 21 recuperator (R113) variables agree within rtol=1e-3 (T10 to 2e-7), including the states at the original's p6 = 3.75e5 kPa = 375 MPa (kept as typed; see README).
